title: Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium Chloride (THPC) Disrupts Lateral Line Hair Cells, Motor Axon Patterning and Larval Locomotion in Zebrafish
content: Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium chloride (THPC) is a phosphonium-salt flame retardant applied to cotton textiles, including children's sleepwear, and a microbiocide in industrial water systems. Neither a brominated compound nor a phosphate ester, it has been largely excluded from flame-retardant screening, and the most recent comprehensive assessment reported adult rodent neurotoxicity but no developmental neurotoxicity data. We exposed zebrafish (Danio rerio, AB strain) embryos to THPC (1–80 mg/L) and measured lethality, hatching, heart rate and morphometry; motor axon, myotome and kinocilium architecture by immunofluorescence; lateral line hair cells by DASPEI labeling with washout; and locomotion in a light/dark paradigm. The 120 h median lethal concentration was 37 mg/L. At 10 and 20 mg/L, THPC suppressed hatching, slowed the heart, restricted growth, enlarged the pericardium and disrupted motor axon patterning. At 1 mg/L (5.2 µM), with no detectable malformation, the myotome was disorganized, neuromast labeling was largely abolished with disrupted kinocilia, and locomotion fell by about 45%. Labeling recovered after washout. THPC is a developmental neurotoxicant well below its lethal threshold.
